name: Porencephaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Porencephaly

criteria.description: Presence of a well-defined cystic cavity within the cerebral hemisphere communicating with the ventricular system or subarachnoid space
Neurological manifestations including hemiparesis, seizures, or developmental delay consistent with lesion location
Confirmation by neuroimaging modalities such as MRI or CT demonstrating characteristic cystic brain lesions
Exclusion of other cystic brain lesions such as schizencephaly or arachnoid cysts

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cystic brain lesion on imaging plus compatible neurological deficits
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on neuroimaging and clinical correlation; genetic testing may be considered in familial cases.

laboratory: CSF analysis usually unremarkable unless secondary infection
imaging: MRI showing cystic cavity within cerebral hemisphere communicating with ventricles
CT scan demonstrating hypodense cystic lesions
Ultrasound in neonates may detect cystic lesions prenatally or postnatally
genetic: Rare familial cases linked to COL4A1 mutations
Genetic testing may identify underlying vascular or connective tissue disorders
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) abnormalities consistent with seizure focus

distinguishingFeatures: Open-lip clefts lined by gray matter on imaging
Bilateral or unilateral clefts extending from ventricle to pial surface
Extra-axial cystic lesion not communicating with ventricles
No associated parenchymal loss or encephalomalacia
Near complete absence of cerebral hemispheres replaced by CSF

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as vomiting and papilledema
references: Barkovich AJ. Pediatric Neuroimaging. 5th ed. Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2012.
